title: A review on enhancing education with AI: exploring the potential of ChatGPT, Bard, and generative AI
extended_summary:
This paper is a review of the role of generative AI in education, focusing on ChatGPT, Bard, and similar large language model-based tools. It asks what benefits these systems may offer to teaching and learning, and what challenges arise when they are introduced into educational settings. The review emphasizes both the promise of generative AI and the need to account for ethical, pedagogical, privacy, and implementation concerns.

The paper does not report a single empirical intervention. Instead, it synthesizes 33 recent peer-reviewed articles selected from 2020–2024, drawn from educational and related journals. The review covers uses such as personalized learning, virtual tutoring, content generation, automated grading, administrative support, and accessibility enhancement. It also discusses concerns including academic integrity, content accuracy, bias, transparency, data privacy, teacher training, equity of access, overreliance on AI, and the need for ongoing adaptation.

The context is broad and international rather than tied to one school level, country, or institution. The article frames generative AI as relevant to students, teachers, curriculum developers, policymakers, and school leaders. Its main conclusion is that generative AI may support education, but responsible adoption requires strong human oversight, professional development, ethical guidelines, privacy protections, and quality assurance mechanisms. The paper is largely conceptual and review-based, so it does not provide direct evidence from classroom implementation or longitudinal use.

identified_tools.name: Gemini
identified_tools.description: Google's generative AI chatbot/model family for conversational text generation and assistance; Bard is a prior name in this family.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper reviews Bard alongside ChatGPT and other generative AI tools in education, discussing potential uses such as personalized learning, content creation, virtual tutoring, and feedback.

findings.finding_summary: This review synthesizes claims and concerns about Bard and similar generative AI in education rather than reporting original empirical results. It highlights potential benefits such as personalized learning, content generation, and automated feedback, but also emphasizes privacy, ethical, pedagogical, and overreliance concerns; no effect sizes or sample sizes are reported.
findings.measure: Narrative review of opportunities and challenges in education

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's conversational generative AI system used for text generation, question answering, tutoring, and feedback.
identified_tools.use_case: The paper reviews ChatGPT as a generative AI tool in education, focusing on its potential roles in personalized learning, virtual tutoring, lesson-plan/content generation, and feedback, along with associated risks.

findings.finding_summary: This review does not present a direct field study of ChatGPT with teachers or instructional coaches. It synthesizes perceived benefits (personalized learning, tutoring, lesson creation, administrative support) and risks including privacy concerns, inaccurate generated content, bias, teacher training needs, and overreliance; no quantitative effect estimates are reported.
findings.measure: Narrative review of opportunities and challenges in education

quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative review article, not a primary empirical study or meta-analysis. It summarizes general claims about generative AI in education without original outcome data, effect sizes, or a teacher/coaching field study.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper discusses potentially important system-level implications for education, including privacy, overreliance, and pedagogical concerns, but it provides no measurable impact estimates. Because there is no empirical effect to assess, the impact is best treated as unclear rather than positive or negative.
